findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions on ec2, s3, lambda and cloudwatch against Resource "*", violating least privilege. A compromise of this user's credentials would allow full control of compute, storage of all buckets, and arbitrary Lambda code execution (including privilege escalation via lambda role passing/EC2 instance profiles).

A permanent IAM access key is created for a human/service user with broad permissions and no PGP key is supplied, so the secret is stored in plaintext in Terraform state. Long-lived static keys cannot be rotated automatically and are a common credential-leak vector; IAM roles or short-lived credentials should be used instead.

The access key secret is exposed through the root module output "secret" without marking it sensitive; because no pgp_key is set, encrypted_secret is empty/unencrypted and the credential material is written to Terraform state and CLI output where it can be read by anyone with state access.

findings.issue_category: IAM user with inline policy instead of group/role
findings.description: Permissions are attached directly to an IAM user via an inline policy rather than through a group or assumable role, which bypasses centralized permission boundaries and makes over-privilege hard to audit or revoke. force_destroy = true also allows silent deletion of the user along with its keys and attached policies.
